idiom_name: pluggable lock policy (type parameter or injected strategy object) plus a scoped-locking guard
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: first write the component without synchronization, then make the synchronization aspect a pluggable policy - a compile-time type parameter where the policy is fixed by the build, an injected strategy object where the deployment decides at run time. Give every member of the policy family the same acquire/release (or lock/unlock) interface, including a no-op strategy for single-threaded configurations, and wrap each critical section in a scoped guard so that release happens on every return and exception path. Keep intra-component calls on unlocked implementation methods (Thread-Safe Interface), so that a non-recursive strategy cannot self-deadlock and no lock is acquired twice.
code_sketch:
component = Component(lock_strategy)         # injected, or a compile-time policy type

def method(component):
    with component.lock_strategy:            # scoped guard: released on every path
        update_state_i(component)            # _i-style: assumes the lock is held
# policy family: mutex | recursive mutex | reader-writer | semaphore | no-op
pitfalls: Treating the strategy as a formality: if any critical section bypasses the guard, the substituted strategy protects nothing.
Swapping strategies without re-checking re-entrancy and lock-ordering assumptions - the plug point cannot encode either.
One strategy instance shared by components with different lock-order requirements, which reintroduces deadlock through the shared policy.

Wrong move: making the strategy interface the union of every lock's features (tryLock, timed acquire, upgrade, downgrade as required members) -> every backend must implement methods it cannot support and callers cannot tell which capabilities exist - the reason the C++ standard library refuses a common virtual base for its mutex types -> instead keep the core contract minimal (lock/unlock or run-under-exclusion) and expose optional capabilities as separate interfaces or traits a consumer can demand, as lock_api's RawMutexTimed/RawRwLockUpgrade extension traits do.

Wrong move: choosing the runtime polymorphic form for hot short critical sections without measuring -> ACE measured roughly 20% overhead from virtual calls for its polymorphic lock interface on top of the acquisition itself, so the pattern becomes a pure regression -> instead use the compile-time policy form so the guard and lock inline, or keep the dynamic form only with profile numbers justifying it.

Wrong move: giving locks a polymorphic base class so a component can store its strategy in place or in shared memory -> virtual bases break value semantics, force heap indirection and make objects with vtables unusable in shared memory, exactly as the ACE_Lock reference warns -> instead parameterize by type, or pass non-owning type-erased views only where run-time variation is genuinely required.
